name: Cassava Root Rot
scientificName: Fusarium solani / Phytophthora spp. / Botryodiplodia theobromae
description: A soil-borne disease complex causing decay of cassava roots, both in the field and during storage. It is favored by waterlogged soils and can cause total yield loss in severely affected fields.
symptoms: Internal root rot with discolored vascular tissue
Soft, foul-smelling decay of harvested roots
Plants may detach easily from soil when pulled
causes: Fusarium solani, Phytophthora spp., Botryodiplodia theobromae fungi
Mechanical damage to roots during weeding
Termite and nematode damage creating entry points
Prolonged drought followed by heavy rainfall
treatments: Remove and destroy infected plants and roots
Harvest infected fields early to reduce spread
Apply lime to adjust soil pH
prevention: Plant on ridges or raised beds to ensure drainage
Avoid damaging roots during field operations
Practice crop rotation with cereals or grasses
Avoid planting cassava in poorly drained fields
